title: Magnetic Effect Of Current
definition: The Magnetic Effect of Current refers to the phenomenon where an electric current flowing through a conductor produces a magnetic field around it, first observed by Hans Christian Oersted in 1820.
importanceInUpsc: This microtopic forms the foundational physics base for understanding electromagnetic induction, electric motors, generators, MRI machines, and particle accelerators, frequently tested in Prelims through direct concept-application questions.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Magnetic Effect Of Current.
